context:

in existing local decisions:
- `move-duckdb-to-optional-extras`
- `isolate-experimental-core-subsystems`
- `remove-release-tooling-from-wheel`

Resolve policy/documentation questions first, then implement any packaging

description:
The 2026-04-01 whole-project pre-Beta review found four release-surface gaps
that should be closed before BenchBox is presented as Beta software:

1. Package metadata already says Beta, but public docs still say Alpha.
2. Install docs contradict the actual dependency model after DuckDB moved to
   optional extras.
3. The default wheel still ships the unsupported `benchbox.experimental`
   namespace without a fully explicit Beta packaging/support policy.
4. `uv run ty check` has too much standing noise to act as a meaningful
   release gate, including warnings on the final execution path in
   `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py`.

This item is about release coherence, not runtime break/fix work. Lint, fast
tests, the wheel/sdist build, and CLI help/version commands are already
passing. The remaining blockers are policy drift, packaging ambiguity, and
release-critical static-analysis noise.

The work must reconcile two completed historical decisions with the current
Beta goal:

- `move-duckdb-to-optional-extras` intentionally made DuckDB non-default.
- `isolate-experimental-core-subsystems` intentionally moved prototypes into
  `benchbox.experimental` but kept them importable from the source tree.

The outcome of this item must be a single coherent Beta support contract
across `pyproject.toml`, canonical docs, built artifacts, and release
verification commands.

anti_patterns.dont: add `benchbox.experimental` to public exports or benchmark registries to make the packaging policy feel simpler
anti_patterns.instead: keep it explicitly unsupported or explicitly out of the default wheel.
anti_patterns.why: that would silently expand the supported Beta surface

anti_patterns.dont: claim DuckDB is part of the default install unless `[project.dependencies]` actually says so
anti_patterns.instead: either change packaging or change docs, but not one without the other.

anti_patterns.dont: try to zero the entire repository-wide `ty` backlog inside this item
anti_patterns.instead: ratchet the release-critical entrypoints first and open follow-up work for the rest.
anti_patterns.why: that turns a focused release blocker into an unbounded cleanup

anti_patterns.instead: update all canonical current-state docs in the same pass.
anti_patterns.why: the FAQ, installation guide, and version-reporting surfaces will drift again

anti_patterns.dont: use `MANIFEST.in` as the mechanism for wheel package exclusion
anti_patterns.why: wheels are controlled by setuptools package discovery/package-data

deferrals.reason: Useful follow-up work, but larger than a Beta-release blocker once the critical gate is ratcheted.
deferrals.summary: Burn down the full repository-wide `ty` backlog outside release-critical entrypoints

deferrals.reason: Potential long-term architecture change; only do this after the immediate Beta packaging policy is stabilized.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Conditional on the default-wheel boundary 'remaining contentious'; Beta packaging policy has since stabilized (item done).
deferrals.summary: Extract benchbox.experimental into a separate distribution if the default-wheel boundary remains contentious

deferrals.reason: Current-state docs and package artifacts are the immediate Beta blocker; historical content can follow.
deferrals.summary: Audit blog posts and historical release summaries for outdated Alpha/install language

preserves.behavior: The completed `move-duckdb-to-optional-extras` rationale is not accidentally reversed by docs-only edits; packaging and docs must agree.
`benchbox.experimental` stays out of `benchbox.__all__` and benchmark registries regardless of whether it remains in or leaves the default wheel.
`benchbox.release` remains excluded from the default wheel.
`uv run -- benchbox --help`, `uv run -- benchbox --version`, and `uv run -- benchbox run --help` continue to exit 0 and expose the current command set.
`uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast -q` remains green after any release-surface cleanup.

scope_rules.path_glob: Benchmark result schema and exported result format contracts
Platform adapter behavior unrelated to packaging/status/install/typecheck cleanup
Supported benchmark registry membership for non-experimental benchmarks

verifications.command: rg -n "Status-Alpha|alpha software|Alpha Software|works with DuckDB out of the box|automatically installed as a dependency" README.md docs/README.md docs/usage/faq.md docs/usage/installation.md docs/platforms/platform-selection-guide.md docs/platforms/duckdb.md
verifications.description: Current-state docs no longer contain stale Alpha/default-DuckDB claims
verifications.expected: No matches for stale current-state status/install claims

verifications.command: uv run ty check benchbox/cli/commands/run.py benchbox/base.py benchbox/__init__.py
verifications.description: Release-critical entrypoints are clean under ty

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/cli/test_cli_package_exports.py tests/unit/cli/test_cli_version_command.py tests/unit/test_version_management.py tests/unit/utils/test_version_markers.py tests/unit/test_release_exclusion_invariants.py tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py -q

verifications.description: Default distribution contents match the documented Beta support policy
verifications.expected: `benchbox/release` absent; `benchbox/experimental` presence or absence matches the documented policy and its tests

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast -q && uv run -- benchbox --help && uv run -- benchbox --version && uv run -- benchbox run --help
verifications.expected: Fast suite passes and all CLI help/version commands exit 0

- Is `benchbox.experimental` part of the default wheel contract?

work_units.notes:
Align release status and scope wording across:
- `pyproject.toml` classifier(s)
- README badge, status section, and contribution/release language
- `docs/README.md`
- `docs/usage/faq.md`
- any other current-state entry docs found in w1

Remove stale Alpha wording and outdated benchmark/platform count claims.
Limit follow-on doc edits to canonical current-state entry points, not

Mixed Alpha/Beta state is not acceptable.
work_units.summary: Resolve alpha/beta and benchmark/platform-count drift across metadata and canonical docs

work_units.notes:
Reconcile all install guidance with the completed
`move-duckdb-to-optional-extras` decision.

Audit and fix contradictory wording in:
- `README.md`
- `docs/usage/faq.md`
- `docs/usage/installation.md`
- `docs/platforms/platform-selection-guide.md`
- `docs/platforms/duckdb.md`
- quick-start/getting-started pages surfaced by w1 if they are canonical
  current-state install entry points under `docs/` or `README.md`

Decide explicitly between:
- keeping DuckDB optional and documenting `--extra duckdb` clearly, or
- intentionally restoring DuckDB to the default dependency surface and
  updating packaging/tests accordingly.

Do not ship hybrid wording such as "works out of the box" while
`pyproject.toml` still keeps DuckDB optional.
work_units.summary: Repair install documentation to match the extras-based DuckDB model or intentionally change the dependency surface

work_units.notes:
Revisit the current outcome of
`isolate-experimental-core-subsystems` and choose one Beta-safe contract:

- Option A: `benchbox.experimental` remains in the default wheel as an
  explicitly unsupported namespace, documented as outside the supported
  product surface.
- Option B: `benchbox.experimental` is removed from the default wheel or
  otherwise moved behind an explicit opt-in distribution/install path.

The chosen contract must cover source-tree imports, wheel installs,
package exports, benchmark registries, docs, and regression tests. This
work unit is the decision point only: record the chosen contract, why the
other option was rejected, and the concrete implementation surfaces that
must change next.
work_units.summary: Choose the Beta packaging and support contract for benchbox.experimental

work_units.notes:
Update only the canonical release surfaces implicated by the w4 decision
so the support boundary is explicit before packaging/test changes land.

Candidate surfaces:
- `README.md`
- `docs/README.md`
- `docs/usage/faq.md`
- `pyproject.toml` classifiers or package metadata comments if they are
  the canonical place to express the support contract

Do not widen this into a repo-wide prose sweep. The goal is a documented,
current-state Beta contract for the shipped package.
work_units.summary: Document the chosen benchbox.experimental contract on canonical release surfaces

work_units.notes:
If Option B is chosen, update setuptools package discovery in
`pyproject.toml` and any wheel/package tests. Do not use `MANIFEST.in`
for wheel exclusion; wheel content is controlled by setuptools package
discovery/package-data, not MANIFEST pruning.

If Option A is chosen, make the support boundary explicit in docs and
tests so the shipped namespace is clearly unsupported but intentionally
present.

In both cases:
- keep `benchbox.release` excluded from the default wheel
- ensure `benchbox.experimental` does not leak into `benchbox.__all__`
  or benchmark registries
- verify wheel contents match the documented policy
work_units.summary: Implement the experimental-boundary packaging decision and add wheel-level invariants

work_units.notes:
Make `ty` actionable on release-critical source files by cleaning the
diagnostics in:
- `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py`
- `benchbox/base.py`
- `benchbox/__init__.py`

Required outcomes:
- no possibly-unresolved `database_config` / `benchmark_config` flow in
  the final orchestration/export/save path
- no unused blanket `type: ignore` suppressions in these files
- control flow in `run.py` is statically obvious enough to support a
  targeted release gate

This is not a mandate to fix all 1200+ repository diagnostics in one
item. The immediate goal is zero noise on release-critical entrypoints.
work_units.summary: Reduce ty diagnostics to zero for Beta-critical entrypoints
